title: How do we regroup so that no count reaches sixty?
description: A count of seventy five sixties is regrouped so that every count is below sixty. Keeko's doubt is that the extra three thousand six hundred can be forgotten.
teaching_notes: One idea: sixty of a landmark make one of the next, so a count of sixty or more is moved up. Watch for students who take sixty sixties out but forget to add one to the next landmark.

source: Regroup (2) × 3600 + (75) × 60 + 10 so that no count is 60 or more.
video_script.why: The child regroups a count that has reached sixty by moving sixty sixties up as one three thousand six hundred, as the book does for seventy sixties.
video_script.substitution: Split the count into sixty and the rest, then add one to the next landmark.
video_script.anchor: the book's base sixty landmarks with a count of seventy five sixties
video_script.wrong_answer: two lots of three thousand six hundred, fifteen sixties and ten
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes sixty sixties out of the count but keeps two lots of 3600, so the value drops by 3600 to 8110
video_script.payoff_line: Three lots of three thousand six hundred, fifteen sixties and ten make the same number.

final_answer.spoken: three lots of three thousand six hundred, fifteen sixties and ten, which is eleven thousand seven hundred ten

maths_rules: 60 sixties = 60 x 60 = 3600, so the 3600s go from 2 to 3
video_script.design: One idea: sixty of the sixties move up as one 3600. The count of 75 splits on the board and the 3600s count goes from two to three.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; (2) x 3600 + (75) x 60 + 10 with the count 75 highlighted and an empty box for the regrouped form

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.sum: (2) x 3600 + (75) x 60 + 10 appears with the count 75 highlighted
marks.ask: an empty box for the regrouped form appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the number system of ancient Mesopotamia.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Here is a number with two lots of three thousand six hundred, seventy five sixties and ten.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must regroup it so that no count is sixty or more. What will the new counts be?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: sixty 60s slide together into one 3600; a count of 60 or more is not allowed

marks.rule: a count of 60 or more is crossed out as not allowed

narration: <bookmark mark='slide'/>Sixty sixties are worth one three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A count can never be sixty or more. Sixty of them move up to the next landmark.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two lots of three thousand six hundred, seventy five sixties and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: the same number with every count below 60

marks.find: the words every count below 60 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the same number with every count below sixty.

marks.split: 75 sixties is split into 60 sixties and 15 sixties

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split the count that is too big. Seventy five sixties are sixty sixties and fifteen sixties.

beats.on_screen: 60 sixties make one 3600, so the 3600s go from 2 to 3

marks.three: the count of 3600s changes from 2 to 3

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>Step two, move the sixty sixties up. They make one more three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The count of three thousand six hundreds goes from two to three.

marks.write: the new form (3) x 3600 + (15) x 60 + 10 is written after the equals sign
marks.below: the counts 3, 15 and 10 are ticked as below 60

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step three, write the new form. The counts are three, fifteen and ten.
<bookmark mark='below'/>Each of them is below sixty, so the regrouping is done.

marks.new: 10800 + 900 + 10 = 11710 is written and both are ticked as equal

narration: <bookmark mark='old'/>Step four, check by value. The old form is seven thousand two hundred, plus four thousand five hundred, plus ten.
<bookmark mark='new'/>That is eleven thousand seven hundred ten. The new form, ten thousand eight hundred plus nine hundred plus ten, gives the same.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three lots of three thousand six hundred, fifteen sixties and ten make the same number.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished regrouping
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's form (2) x 3600 + (15) x 60 + 10 with the label 7200 + 900 + 10 = 8110; the missing 3600 shown as a gap; the 3600s count corrected from 2 to 3

marks.read: the label 7200 + 900 + 10 = 8110 appears next to 11710 with a gap of 3600
marks.fix: the count of 3600s is corrected from 2 to 3

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it is two lots of three thousand six hundred, fifteen sixties and ten. Only the count of sixties needed to change, says Keeko.
<bookmark mark='read'/>That form is worth eight thousand one hundred ten, which is three thousand six hundred too small.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The sixty sixties we took out did not vanish. They became one more three thousand six hundred, so the two becomes three.
